intro: A plain roundup of the week's notable military and business technology (full analysis was unavailable this run).

deep_dives.title: US Army, Kaizen Laboratories to establish common software platform for classified material
deep_dives.what_happened: The U.S. Army recently awarded $43 million to Kaizen Laboratories to create application software for highly sensitive military material.

deep_dives.title: Lockheed Martin unveils PAC-3 Edge interceptor designed to counter hypersonic threats
deep_dives.what_happened: Lockheed Martin said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls and a multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman.

deep_dives.title: Bunker Talk: Let’s Talk About All The Things We Did And Didn’t Cover This Week
deep_dives.what_happened: The throw rug really pulls the bunker together, don't you think? The post Bunker Talk: Let’s Talk About All The Things We Did And Didn’t Cover This Week appeared first on TWZ .

deep_dives.title: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply
deep_dives.what_happened: The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.

deep_dives.title: Coast Guard places $248 million order for first MQ-9B drones
deep_dives.what_happened: The unarmed drones are meant to “give the Coast Guard crews a longer-range view of our maritime domain,” a senior official said.

deep_dives.title: One year in, Army’s FUZE leader eyes ‘bigger’ acquisition challenges
deep_dives.what_happened: The Army innovation hub’s first year also revealed the challenge of making sure promising technologies don’t stop at the prototype stage, FUZE Director Matt Willis told Breaking Defense.

deep_dives.title: Lockheed unveils PAC-3 Edge, its next-gen Patriot interceptor
deep_dives.what_happened: The aerospace giant intends to invest hundreds of millions of dollars of its own cash in the missile alone, alongside additional investments in its seeker and solid rocket motor, said Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed’s missiles and fire control division.

deep_dives.title: Drones and autonomous warfare: ‘One-way attack’ and reshaping ISR
deep_dives.what_happened: [Sponsored] Systems that can work independently while still being part of a unit are critical to carrying out multi-domain operations.
